description: Minimum Tauri permissions the webview actually uses. The Rust host owns the Go sidecar lifecycle (spawn/kill via std::process — no shell plugin needed); the webview invokes two custom commands (get_backend_config, restart_backend) plus opens external URLs via shellOpen. Spawn/kill/execute were previously granted and represented pure gratuitous authority an XSS payload would inherit. NOTE: shell:allow-open is deliberately UNSCOPED — the same call site handles https URLs (device-auth verification_uri) and bare filesystem paths (reveal-in-explorer), and no single validator covers both without breaking one. Residual risk (documented, accepted): a compromised backend could direct the desktop app to open arbitrary URIs via the OS handler. If reveal moves to a dedicated Rust command, scope this to https://**.
